header.tag_why: The CFO accepted the cost-of-manual-matching case once it was built from her own statements, which turned a stalled deal into a signature.

messaging_changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
messaging_changes.change: For finance owners (CFOs, controllers): "Know where every deposit is, and see each one matched to its transactions and invoices." Lead with this. Move M1 to a later slide.
messaging_changes.why: Our opener drew silence and the CFO only engaged when the reconciliation demo showed her own deposits, and she said "I just want to know where my money is" rather than using any infrastructure language.

messaging_changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
messaging_changes.change: "We'll calculate your cost of manual deposit matching from your own statements, and show the method so you can check every input." Use this as a standard ROI session, not a published figure.
messaging_changes.why: The CFO asked to see the analysis on her own data, and her reply "that's my number, not yours" shows that a generic study does not persuade, while the rep could not reproduce the figure that closed the deal.

messaging_changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
messaging_changes.change: Stop leading with developer messaging for finance buyers in B2B deals. Use it only when a technical buyer is the decider.
messaging_changes.why: The decider was the finance owner, who never said "payments" and signed on a close and deposit-matching problem, while the developer-first message had no role in the decision.

messaging_changes.change: For wholesale and distribution buyers: "A wholesale distributor reference, with a reference call booked before the proposal." Do not send retail case studies to B2B distributors.
messaging_changes.why: The CFO asked for a distributor reference and dismissed the retail case study we sent instead, and the reference call was never delivered, so a matching proof point is missing from our messaging.

trigger.insight: The inbound was about a portal, but the real trigger was a new CFO's nine-day close and two people hand-matching deposits in spreadsheets. The rep's first read was wrong, and the first proposal was built on the wrong problem.
trigger.messaging: Lead with the month-end close and manual deposit matching, not the portal, checkout or infrastructure.

decider.insight: Paul said outright that Ines decides, and she signed. The team pitched the IT director first and never got the CFO into the room, so the first proposal sat for three weeks until she dismissed it as not her problem.
decider.messaging: Target the finance owner in the first conversation and make the first asset speak to their close, not to IT.

competitor.messaging: Frame the switch around the cost of unmatched deposits and manual close, not rate comparisons.

message.insight: Our standard opener drew silence, and the reconciliation demo drew the CFO's stop-and-redirect. The CFO responded to a payout-to-transaction tie-out on her own data, not to the infrastructure story that M1 leads with.
message.messaging: Move M9 (every payout reconciles automatically to its transactions and your ERP) to the opener and demote M1 to a later slide.

decided.insight: The rep had the deal at 20 percent and called it dead before the statement analysis, so the win came from the CFO asking for her own data, not from the pipeline. The dollar figure that closed it is unverified: the rep can't recall the exact number, so it can't be relied on as proof.
decided.messaging: Make a run-it-on-your-statements ROI session a standard step, with the calculation documented so the customer can check it.

gaps.insight: The CFO asked for a wholesale distributor reference and we sent a retail case study, which she dismissed. We never delivered the call, and she signed anyway, so the gap is still open. The counter-sales card reader question was answered with a slide, so whether the 14 branches are in scope is unconfirmed.
gaps.messaging: Build a wholesale and distribution reference before the next pitch and stop sending retail case studies to B2B distributors.

language.insight: The customer described money location, deposits and manual close, and never used payments or infrastructure. Our category words are not in her vocabulary, so M1 and M2 describe our product in terms she doesn't use.
language.messaging: Rewrite the opener around knowing where every deposit is and matching it to transactions and invoices, in the customer's own words.

gaps.question: Was the 14-branch counter-sales card reader reporting in the signed scope, and was Wen's slide claim verified?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Wen whether the counter readers feed the same report, and ask Dana whether the contract or order form covers the 14 branches.

gaps.question: What did Fiserv or the bank actually pitch, beyond the rate comparison?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Ines directly, or Paul, what the bank offered and what they said about the switch.

gaps.question: What was the exact ROI figure and how was it calculated?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Wen to reconstruct the calculation from the controller's statements and confirm the hours and cost inputs.

gaps.question: Was the distributor reference call ever scheduled or delivered?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Dana whether a reference call was ever booked and who owns distributor references on the customer success team.

close.rep_takeaway: Get the finance owner into the first conversation and lead with a reconciliation demo on their own data, not the deck or the portal. Don't cite a dollar figure you can't reproduce, and don't close a deal with an open reference request.
